sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunoprecipitation confirmed extracellular FLAG display; receptor ligand-binding function not measured because the ectodomain is absent in this construct.
sites.rationale: The FLAG-EphA4-ΔE construct retains the signal peptide, transmembrane domain, and intracellular kinase domain but lacks the ectodomain (residues 20–548). The FLAG tag is therefore placed at the sole extracellular face of this construct — the mature N-terminus immediately after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 19 (A), before residue 20 (V). No specific junction residue is named in the paper, so the position is topology-derived: with the ectodomain deleted, exactly one extracellular terminus exists. The tag is 530 residues from the TM boundary (549), satisfying the ≥3-residue constraint. Python confirmed residue_before = A (pos 19) and residue_after = V (pos 20). FLAG-EphA4-ΔE is a membrane-anchored construct (stably expressed in HEK293 cells) in which the ectodomain is deleted and a FLAG tag is placed on the extracellular face; surface immunoprecipitation and detection of secreted peptides confirmed extracellular display of the FLAG epitope.

sources.claim:
The generation of the constructs and oligonucleotides used is described in Tables S1 and S2
HEK293 cells stably expressing human FLAG‐EphA4‐ΔE (FLAG‐A4ΔE), FLAG‐EphB2‐ΔE (FLAG‐B2ΔE), FLAG‐E‐cadherin‐ΔE (FLAG‐CadΔE) and FLAG‐C55 were cultured in Dulbecco´s modified Eagle's medium supplemented with 10% FBS and 400 µg/ml G418 or 200 µg/ml hygromycin.

literature_notes: L2 (N-terminal myc tag on ephrin-B3) was considered but disqualified: ephrin-B3 is the ligand for EphA4, not a close ortholog of EphA4 (receptor vs. ligand, different protein families — EphB-class ligand vs. EphA-class receptor). It provides no positional precedent for EphA4 tagging. L1 supports one site only: the mature N-terminus of the FLAG-EphA4-ΔE construct. The position is topology-derived because the paper names no specific junction residue; the ΔE deletion leaves exactly one extracellular face. Validation is surface_only: surface IP confirmed extracellular display, but ephrin-binding function cannot be assessed in the ΔE background. No internal extracellular loop sites are supported by the ledger.
